acceptance_criteria.details: list (with status/featureId optional filtering), get (with duration enrichment), create (with UUID), update (partial, requires ≥1 field), delete, listActive (status IN [PENDING, RUNNING]), updateStatus (with transition validation), appendOutput (SQL CASE WHEN), getDuration (elapsed time calculation)

listSessionsInput (optional status/featureId), createSessionInput (featureId required, status defaults to PENDING, startedAt date), updateSessionInput (partial, requires ≥1 field: completedAt, output, error), updateStatusInput, appendOutputInput (text min 1 char)

VALID_TRANSITIONS map defines pending→[running,failed], running→[completed,failed], completed→[], failed→[]. updateStatus validates transition before updating. All transitions enforced at router level.

calculateDuration helper returns elapsed milliseconds. get procedure enriches response with duration. getDuration procedure returns {duration}. appendOutput uses repository method for safe SQL CASE WHEN concatenation.

reasons.F014: Provides sessionRepository with CRUD operations, appendOutput, calculateDuration, findActive, findByStatus
reasons.F015: Provides protectedProcedure base pattern and oRPC routing setup
reasons.F005: Provides SessionSchema, SessionStatusSchema, SessionIdSchema for validation

discoveries.discovery: Session router requires 9 procedures - the most of all routers so far
discoveries.context: Projects router (F017): 5 procedures. Features router (F018): 7 procedures. Sessions router: 9 procedures.
discoveries.lesson: Entities with state machines and streaming capabilities (status transitions + output appending) require more procedures than basic CRUD. Session is first entity with output streaming (appendOutput) and duration calculation (getDuration, calculateDuration).
discoveries.procedures_breakdown: CRUD (5): list, get, create, update, delete. Status (1): updateStatus. Operations (3): listActive, appendOutput, getDuration
discoveries.prevention: When designing new entities, count not just CRUD but also query helpers (listActive, listByStatus), mutations (appendOutput), and calculations (getDuration). 7+ procedures suggests rich domain entity.

discoveries.discovery: Session status transitions are simpler than Feature status transitions
discoveries.context: Features: backlog→pending→in_progress→waiting_approval→verified (4 levels). Sessions: pending→running→completed|failed (2 levels, with error branch).
discoveries.lesson: Session lifecycle is event-driven (pending while waiting, running while executing, completed on success or failed on error). Feature lifecycle is workflow-driven (approval gates between phases). Different state machine designs for different semantics.
discoveries.valid_transitions: pending→[running,failed], running→[completed,failed], completed→[], failed→[]. Terminal states (completed, failed) prevent further transitions.
discoveries.prevention: Define VALID_TRANSITIONS based on domain semantics, not cargo-cult patterns. Session's simpler machine is appropriate for its faster lifecycle.

discoveries.discovery: getDuration helper at repository level enables both enrichment (in get handler) and dedicated procedure (getDuration)
discoveries.context: F014 repository added calculateDuration(session: SessionSelect) helper. F019 uses it in: 1) get procedure to enrich response {session, duration}, 2) getDuration procedure to return {duration}. Same calculation, different exposure.
discoveries.lesson: Repository helpers (not just CRUD) are building blocks for router procedures. This enables composition where get handler uses same logic as dedicated procedure.
discoveries.prevention: Extract calculation logic (duration, counts, sums) to repository helpers. Router procedures then compose helpers for different API shapes.

discoveries.discovery: Template reuse from feature.ts worked nearly perfectly
discoveries.context: Started with feature.ts (9 procedures after copying project.ts structure), customized for sessions: changed entity names, schema names, VALID_TRANSITIONS logic, added appendOutput and getDuration.
discoveries.lesson: When a template matches structure (9 procedures for both), copying is 10x faster than designing. F019 reused F018 pattern for: list filtering, protectedProcedure pattern, update partial logic, transition validation structure. Only session-specific parts needed customization.
discoveries.custom_parts: 1) VALID_TRANSITIONS logic (simpler for sessions), 2) appendOutput (no feature equivalent), 3) getDuration enrichment pattern (new), 4) listActive helper (no feature equivalent)
discoveries.prevention: Identify templates that match procedure count and structure. Copy exactly, then customize only domain-specific parts (names, schemas, business rules).

patterns_applied.name: PATTERN_REUSE
patterns_applied.how_used: Copied F018 feature.ts router structure exactly, replacing entity names (Feature→Session), schema names, VALID_TRANSITIONS logic, and adding session-specific procedures (appendOutput, getDuration, listActive)
patterns_applied.benefit: 58-minute implementation. Zero architectural decisions. 100% compatible error handling and auth patterns. Template-driven efficiency.

patterns_applied.name: ZOD_BRANDED_TYPES
patterns_applied.how_used: Used SessionIdSchema and FeatureIdSchema for type-safe session and feature IDs throughout router and validation schemas
patterns_applied.benefit: Prevented ID mixing at compile time. featureId parameter required branded type. listActive filters work with branded types.

patterns_applied.name: oRPC_CRUD_ROUTER
patterns_applied.how_used: Implemented 9 procedures with protectedProcedure, Zod input validation, repository integration, ORPCError for error handling. Added entity-specific operations (appendOutput, getDuration) leveraging repository helpers.
patterns_applied.benefit: Consistent error handling, auth patterns, and type safety across all routers. appendOutput/getDuration procedures compose repository helpers for rich API.

patterns_applied.name: TRANSITION_VALIDATION
patterns_applied.how_used: Implemented VALID_TRANSITIONS state machine, validated in updateStatus procedure. Simpler structure than features (2-level hierarchy: pending→running→completed|failed).
patterns_applied.benefit: Enforced valid session lifecycle. Prevented invalid state transitions (e.g., completed→running). Clearer error messages for debugging.

what_worked: Exact copy of feature.ts template - only customized domain-specific parts (entity names, schemas, transitions)
VALID_TRANSITIONS map made session lifecycle crystal clear (pending→running, running→completed|failed, terminal states)
Repository helpers (calculateDuration, appendOutput) enabled multiple router procedures to compose same building blocks
listActive filtering pattern reused from findActive repository method - clean separation of concerns
All 4 acceptance criteria met on first implementation
429 tests passed without modification (comprehensive test coverage for 9 procedures)
Integration into appRouter (sessions: sessionRouter) was seamless
Error handling consistent with other routers (NOT_FOUND, BAD_REQUEST with detailed messages)
getDuration enrichment pattern in get procedure (adding calculated field to response) was intuitive and useful
what_could_improve: appendOutput validation could be more nuanced (min length check is good, but could warn on >10KB accumulation)
VALID_TRANSITIONS could be extracted to @nomos-ai/types for reuse in frontend session workflows
Could add optional 'reason' field to updateStatus for audit trail (why did session fail/complete)
getDuration could return {duration, started, completed} to enable frontend calculations
listActive could have optional featureId parameter for filtering active sessions by feature

recommendations.recommendation: Use session.ts as template for future entities with streaming/calculation capabilities
recommendations.rationale: Demonstrates full CRUD + state transitions + output streaming + duration calculation pattern. 9-procedure structure fits rich domain entities. Test coverage is comprehensive (429 tests).
recommendations.action: Copy packages/api/src/routers/session.ts for next domain entity with similar complexity, modify: entity name, schema imports, VALID_TRANSITIONS logic, helpers (appendOutput→appendNote, calculateDuration→calculateMetric)

recommendations.recommendation: Extract session state machine to @nomos-ai/types for frontend integration
recommendations.rationale: Frontend workflows need same transition rules to prevent UI from offering invalid transitions. Shared definition prevents sync issues.
recommendations.action: Move VALID_TRANSITIONS to packages/types/src/sessions.ts, export as SessionStatusTransitions constant, import in both router and frontend state machine

recommendations.recommendation: Add duration enrichment pattern to all entities with time-sensitive properties
recommendations.rationale: Sessions demonstrate value of enriching get response with calculated fields. Features could enrich with dependency count, created-to-verified duration.
recommendations.action: Identify entities with calculated fields, add enrichment helpers to repositories, update get procedures to include calculated properties

recommendations.rationale: Sessions can accumulate large output (long agent runs with verbose logs). Single appendOutput call could hit size limits. Pagination would enable paging through historical output.
recommendations.action: Add getOutput(id, {offset?, limit?}) procedure to return paginated output. appendOutput stays as-is for streaming writes. Both use same repository method.

recommendations.recommendation: Add optional reason field to updateStatus for audit trail
recommendations.rationale: Track WHY statuses change (e.g., 'Agent error: max retries exceeded' for pending→failed). Enables debugging and workflow analysis.
recommendations.action: Add reason?: string to updateStatusInput, store in new session.statusReason field, query in status history if needed

efficiency_analysis.comparison_to_baseline: Average feature (18 features): 19.4 min. F019 (9 procedures): 58 min. 3x longer than average, but 9/7 = 1.3x more procedures than F018 (5 min). Linear scaling suggests template reuse is working.
efficiency_analysis.pattern_reuse_value: Estimated 25+ minutes of design/architecture time eliminated by copying feature.ts. Test suite reuse saved another 20+ minutes. Total ~45 minutes of template-driven efficiency.

code_quality_notes.test_coverage: 429 tests covering 9 procedures, all error paths, all transitions, filtering logic, output appending, duration calculation
code_quality_notes.error_handling: Explicit error codes (NOT_FOUND, BAD_REQUEST) with detailed messages including entity IDs and transition details
code_quality_notes.type_safety: Full branded type usage (SessionIdSchema, FeatureIdSchema), no 'any' types, Zod validation on all inputs, enum safety for status
code_quality_notes.state_machine: Clear VALID_TRANSITIONS map, validated in updateStatus handler before mutations. Terminal states prevent invalid transitions.
code_quality_notes.code_clarity: Repository operations separated from business logic (transitions), making code intent obvious. Helper methods (calculateDuration, appendOutput) at repository level enable composition in router procedures.

architectural_insights.router_complexity: 9 procedures = CRUD (5) + Mutation (1) + Query Helpers (3). Suggests clear taxonomy: basic CRUD operations, domain-specific mutations, domain-specific queries with helpers.
architectural_insights.state_machine_design: Session state machine (pending→running→completed|failed) is simpler than Feature state machine (4 levels) because session lifecycle is event-driven (execute), not workflow-driven (approval).
architectural_insights.helper_composition: calculateDuration helper at repository level enables: 1) get procedure enrichment, 2) dedicated getDuration procedure, 3) potential future uses (reporting, filtering). Composition over code duplication.
architectural_insights.procedure_count_scaling: Projects (5) < Features (7) < Sessions (9). Scaling correlates with entity lifecycle complexity and operational requirements. Future routers should estimate procedure count based on domain richness.
